# Results — Study 761 (Hotel-RevPAR)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Hotel **RevPAR** (Revenue Per
Available Room) — the lodging industry's headline demand gauge, published monthly by STR /
CoStar — tested as a **leading** signal for hotel REITs. STR's monthly series is
proprietary, so we use a **clearly-labelled approximate reconstruction** anchored to
STR/CoStar-reported **annual** U.S. RevPAR, with the 2020 COVID collapse and 2021 recovery
set to the reported national monthly path. We align it to **HST** (Host Hotels & Resorts,
the flagship lodging REIT) and to an equal-weight lodging-REIT basket, and ask whether
RevPAR YoY momentum **leads** the hotel tape. Offline & deterministic; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| RevPAR tape | monthly U.S. hotel RevPAR ($), **hardcoded PROXY** anchored to STR/CoStar-reported annual RevPAR (COVID months = reported national path) |
| Hotel tape | yfinance **HST** daily total-return close (`auto_adjust`), month-end; robustness = equal-weight lodging-REIT basket (HST, RHP, SHO, DRH, PEB, APLE, PK) |
| Window | 1998-01-31 → 2026-05-31 (**341** month-ends; **28.3** years); as-of **2026-07-13** |
| Signal | RevPAR **YoY log momentum** `m_t = log(RevPAR_t / RevPAR_{t-12})` (YoY differencing kills hotel seasonality); UPCYCLE = `m_t > 0` |
| Momentum stats | mean **+0.033**, std **0.244**, fraction of months > 0 ≈ **77%** |
| Entry / lag / costs | STR releases month-`t` RevPAR ~mid-`t+1`; enter at close of `t+1` (**1-month release lag**); timing overlay charges 10 bps one-way per turn; hotel tape total-return |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** RevPAR here is an approximate
> reconstruction, not STR's licensed tape. The verdict rides on the travel cycle's **YoY
> shape** — which the annual anchors and the reported COVID path pin down — and on the
> **direction** of the lead-lag relationship, not on any single month's exact dollar
> figure. Both HST and the lodging basket give the same sign and significance, so the
> conclusion does not hinge on the proxy's exact weights.

## The signal — forward hotel returns after an UPCYCLE month (RevPAR YoY > 0) vs base

1-month release lag; the unconditional column is *all* overlapping forward windows over the
same tape (the honest base rate). Welch *t* compares the UPCYCLE conditional mean to the
unconditional mean. **HAC *t*** is the slope of a predictive regression of the forward
return on RevPAR momentum, with Newey-West (Bartlett) standard errors at the overlap
length — the direct "does momentum *lead*?" test. The placebo *p* is the share of 20,000
random same-size date draws whose mean forward return **beats** the UPCYCLE set.

| horizon | n UPCYCLE | UPCYCLE mean | DOWNCYCLE mean | base mean | UPCYCLE win | Welch *t* | HAC β | **HAC *t*** | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 263 | +1.13% | +0.11% | +0.90% | 54% | +0.31 | −0.022 | **−0.91** | 0.355 |
| 3-month  | 262 | +2.84% | +2.14% | +2.68% | 60% | +0.12 | −0.076 | **−1.44** | 0.437 |
| 6-month  | 259 | +5.07% | +5.58% | +5.18% | 63% | −0.06 | −0.169 | **−2.31** | 0.515 |
| 12-month | 253 | +7.75% | **+16.52%** | +9.75% | 62% | −0.80 | −0.291 | **−2.77** | 0.817 |

Read it carefully. The "ride the travel cycle" story wants a *large, positive, significant*
lead: UPCYCLE months should pay **more** than base. Instead the excess is **essentially
zero at 1–3 months** (Welch *t* = 0.3 / 0.1), and by 6–12 months it **inverts** — the HAC
slope is significantly **negative** (*t* = −2.3 at 6m, **−2.8** at 12m), and forward
12-month returns after a "boom" (RevPAR growing YoY) average **+7.8%** versus **+16.5%**
after a "bust" month. A high RevPAR YoY is a **late-cycle** tell, not a buy signal: by the
time the industry is reporting fat year-on-year gains, the easy hotel-equity returns are
behind you. The claimed positive lead is not there.

## Lead-lag — the hotel equity *leads* RevPAR, not the reverse

Correlation of RevPAR momentum at *t* with the hotel return over `[t+L, t+L+1]`. `L < 0`
means momentum **lags** the equity (the stock moved first); `L > 0` means momentum
**leads** it. A genuine leading indicator peaks at `L > 0`.

| lead *L* (months) | −6 | −3 | 0 | +3 | +6 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| corr(momentum, return) | **+0.087** | +0.062 | −0.047 | −0.052 | −0.076 |

The correlation is **positive at negative leads and negative at positive leads**, peaking
at **L = −6**. In plain terms: the hotel stock moves **~6 months before** the RevPAR print
turns — exactly what a forward-looking claim on future room revenue should do. RevPAR is a
**coincident-to-lagging** confirmation of what the equity already discounted, not an early
warning. The leading-indicator arrow points backwards.

## Tradability — a long-when-growing overlay tops buy-and-hold, but on ~2 regime calls

Long HST when RevPAR YoY > 0 (known one month earlier), else flat (long/flat) or short
(long/short). 10 bps one-way per turn; hotel tape total-return; flat leg earns 0 (a
conservative simplification that *flatters* the timing rule).

| rule | exposure | turns | net ann. return | **net Sharpe** | buy-&-hold Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **long / flat** | 77% | 8 | +10.3% | **0.45** | **0.31** |
| **long / short** | 100% | 17 | +9.4% | **0.26** | **0.31** |

The long/flat overlay *does* beat buy-and-hold (net Sharpe **0.45 vs 0.31**; $1 → **9.0×**
vs **4.2×**). But look at **turns = 8** over **28 years**: this is a slow filter that makes
only ~4 round-trips, and its whole edge is **sitting out the two great hotel crashes**
(2008–09 and 2020, when RevPAR YoY went deeply negative and HST fell ~70% / ~50%). That is
**two regime episodes**, not a repeatable predictive edge — and because the equity *leads*
the gauge (above), in real time RevPAR YoY only turns negative *after* the stock has
already dropped, so the overlay de-risks late. It is a crash/volatility filter resting on a
couple of events, not a signal. **FRAGILE**, not investable.

## Robustness — the sign is stable in the threshold and in the basket

| UPCYCLE threshold | n | UPCYCLE 12m mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −0.05 (loose) | 283 | +6.8% | −1.15 | −2.77 |
| **0.0** (sign) | 253 | +7.7% | −0.80 | −2.77 |
| +0.05 (strict) | 160 | +8.8% | −0.35 | −2.77 |
| +0.10 (booming) | 33 | +5.7% | −1.07 | −2.77 |

(The HAC *t* is the continuous-slope regression and does not depend on the discretization
threshold.) There is **no threshold** at which UPCYCLE months pay a positive, significant
excess. On the **equal-weight lodging-REIT basket** the story is if anything *sharper*: 12m
UPCYCLE mean **+7.3%** vs base **+10.8%**, HAC *t* = **−3.67** (6m HAC *t* = −2.93). Same
sign, same significance — not a single-stock artefact.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and a flat signal stays flat

On a deterministic monthly series (a slow travel cycle × fixed seasonality for RevPAR, a
REIT-sized price), with a **planted** forward lead (next month's return lifted when RevPAR
momentum is positive):

| planted edge | n UPCYCLE | UPCYCLE 6m | base 6m | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 142 | +5.06% | +6.59% | −0.88 | **+0.28** | 0.845 |
| **0.03** (large edge) | 142 | +23.68% | +15.76% | +3.62 | **+5.02** | **0.000** |

With **no** planted edge the HAC *t* sits at **+0.28** (no false positive from a noisy
cyclical signal); a genuine planted lead drives it to **+5.02** and the placebo *p* to
**0.000**. The inference recovers a real positive lead **when one exists** — so the
real-tape result (positive-lead *t* ≈ 0 short, significantly *negative* long) is a true
absence of the claimed signal, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claim is that RevPAR momentum **positively leads** hotel REITs. It
  does not: the positive-lead HAC *t* is ~0 at 1–3 months (−0.9 / −1.4) and turns
  significantly **negative** at 6–12 months (−2.3 / **−2.8**), i.e. a high RevPAR YoY
  *precedes lower* forward returns (12m: +7.8% after a boom vs +16.5% after a bust). The
  only significant relationship runs the **wrong way** for the claim — a late-cycle
  mean-reversion echo (partly mechanical: two cyclical series, overlapping windows, a
  proxy tape), not a leading buy signal. Fails the *t* ≥ 2 bar **in the claimed direction**.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** A long-when-RevPAR-growing overlay *does* top buy-and-hold in
  sample (net Sharpe 0.45 vs 0.31; 9.0× vs 4.2×), but only as a slow crash/volatility
  filter resting on **8 switches / ~2 regime episodes** over 28 years, with **no positive
  predictive content** and **lagging execution** (the equity leads the gauge). Thin,
  event-driven, and not a repeatable edge.
- **Leading indicator? — BUSTED.** The lead-lag correlation peaks at **L = −6** (positive
  where momentum *lags* the equity, negative at every positive lead): the hotel stock moves
  ~6 months **before** RevPAR turns. RevPAR is a coincident-to-lagging confirmation of the
  travel cycle, not the early read the folklore sells.
